newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Air NZ silent on possible SIA tie.
newsitem.headline: Air NZ silent on possible SIA tie.

text.p: Air New Zealand Ltd declined to comment on a report in Friday's Independent Business Weekly that it is close to a tie-up with Singapore Airlines.

The Independent said the tie-up was likely to involve Singapore Airlines buying some, if not all, of Qantas Airways' 19.4 percent stake after Air NZ's entry to Australia through 50 percent ownership of Ansett Holdings.
Qantas' stake in Air NZ is worth about NZ$318 million.
Air NZ spokesman David Beatson told the Independent the company would announce an alliance with another airline in either Asia, the United States or Europe within weeks.
"Now that we have secured the Ansett arrangement, we are looking at how we can capitalise on that," he said.
Air NZ spokeswoman Jane-Frances O'Halloran told Reuters Beatson had been quoted correctly, but that there would be no further comment.

At the annual meeting early this month, Chairman Bob Matthew said Air NZ was close to concluding comprehensive commercial alliance agreements with other leading international airlines but gave no indication that they would involve equity.

"These major developments are expected to deliver substantial benefits to the company, though it will be six months or so before the major benefits from these arrangements start to come to account," he said.
